scope: Original human recordings only; follow-up research, not installed-model changes

common.segregation: Reference-only views by split and intent; keep true UNKNOWN, ambiguous references, isolated tokens, synthetic and constructed speech separate
common.sampling: 75% human positives / 25% true human negatives; positive intent -> typed command -> source -> speaker -> recording; negative coarse family -> rejection reason -> source -> speaker -> recording
common.segmentation: Preserve original audio; energy screens only propose outer boundaries with 150 ms context. Never concatenate words, remove internal pauses, or declare an energy threshold to be ground-truth VAD
common.preprocessing: Verify WAV/PCM/feature hashes, mono 16 kHz, finite float32 40-bin features, runtime length and repeated-label CTC feasibility. Refit normalization on exactly admitted human train rows; reuse transforms in development/runtime
common.normalization_ablation: Frozen train-only global normalization is the baseline. Per-utterance mean/variance normalization is a separately versioned train/dev ablation, never an untested inference-only replacement
common.pretraining: Start from random acoustic weights for a genuine human-only baseline. Do not call synthetic-exposed targeted-v7 or v10 checkpoints human-only. Isolated original-human tokens may become a separately audited training-only auxiliary experiment; no concatenation or connected-command coverage claim
common.splits: Preserve published membership. Audit every split pair for declared and source speaker, byte/PCM hash, paired recording, session and parent IDs. Physical-speaker aliases and perceptual near-duplicates need independent review. New blind evaluation requires new people/sessions
common.speaker_target_interpretation: Per typed command, disjoint speakers across splits; pilot collection floors only, not statistically sufficient quality certification. Repeated recordings and TTS voices do not increase human-speaker coverage
common.selection: Human development complete-command macro-intent and macro-speaker recall with precision/FAR constraints; no mixed-phase bonus, pooled synthetic selection or test-driven threshold changes
common.calibration: Fit only on original human dev/calibration; missing human evidence blocks an intent-specific readiness claim. Keep required-slot/target checks. Report raw recognition, accepted correct, wrong accepts, abstentions and true-negative FAR separately
common.evaluation: All 18 finite intents plus UNKNOWN and ambiguous-reference counts; command, slot, source, speaker and acoustic-condition breakdowns. Existing published test/holdout are regression evidence, not a new blind test
common.annotation_review: Publisher dataset labels, folder prompts and ASR-derived transcripts remain distinct provenance strata. Do not treat any as independently listened ground truth. Human reviewers verify command, all slots, boundaries, negation and uncertainty; hash-bind decisions and rebuild every dependent target together

PLAY_MUSIC.collection: Record generic play/start/put-on variants from independent speakers. Collect complete title-only and title-plus-artist utterances for each approved catalog item before claiming named-music support
PLAY_MUSIC.review: Do not collapse unknown title/artist or incomplete play-song-number requests to generic playback. Keep arbitrary names out of scope
contrasts: PLAY_MUSIC vs NEXT: play music / play next song
generic play vs known song vs unknown song
PLAY_MUSIC.segmentation: Retain utterance-final title and artist; score generic and named music separately
PLAY_MUSIC.auxiliary: Human name/token enrollment is training-only with independent command evaluation; it is not an ASR fallback

WEATHER.collection: Add weather/query paraphrases across sources and household microphones, not repeated takes from one source speaker
WEATHER.review: Weather intent detection does not establish arbitrary question-answering or external factual answers
contrasts: supported query vs negated or multi-action query
WEATHER.segmentation: Retain initial whats/how-is and final today/outside; compare complete waveform and actual neural endpoint without changing labels
WEATHER.auxiliary: No threshold selected by inspecting weather test confidences

TIME.collection: Record time/current-time paraphrases, short Time, and polite connected queries across speakers
TIME.review: Review foreign-location/timezone and date requests against the fixed schema; never silently erase an unsupported qualifier
contrasts: supported local time vs unsupported date/location context
TIME.segmentation: Protect short Time and initial consonants; a global minimum-duration rule must not remove valid commands
TIME.auxiliary: Time-word clips do not establish connected clock-time recognition

LIGHT_ON.collection: Fill every generic/kitchen/bedroom/bathroom target with independent speakers and multiple turn-on/power-on/light-on phrasings
LIGHT_ON.review: Rebuild the binary target label as named=1, generic=0 from typed light_id. Do not use a generic-target prior to hide named-target failures
contrasts: on vs off for the same target
turn on vs do not turn on
LIGHT_ON.segmentation: Protect short on polarity and trailing room names; no polarity-token masking in the human-only baseline
LIGHT_ON.auxiliary: Balance target and source within intent; repeated generic-light clips are not named-light evidence

LIGHT_OFF.collection: Fill generic and named targets with shut-off/lights-out/kill-lights variants from separate speakers
LIGHT_OFF.review: Keep light-off distinct from stop/turn-off-the-music and unknown appliance control
contrasts: off vs on for each light target
LIGHT_OFF.segmentation: Preserve final off and target words; inspect clipped trailing fricatives rather than aggressively trimming
LIGHT_OFF.auxiliary: Use the same named/generic target mapping as LIGHT_ON and brightness/color

PAUSE.collection: Record single-word Pause and pause-audio/song variants across speakers, rooms and distances
PAUSE.review: Do not merge pause and stop solely because an action binding behaves similarly
contrasts: pause audio vs pause an unsupported operation
PAUSE.segmentation: Keep brief utterances and onset consonants; review short clips with adequate CTC output frames
PAUSE.auxiliary: Short-word auxiliary clips remain separate from connected commands

STOP.collection: Add stop/end-playback/turn-off-music variants across sources and capture conditions
STOP.review: Distinguish media stop from cancel-timer, stop-calling, negated stop and unrelated conversational stop
STOP.segmentation: Protect a brief Stop; do not drop clips solely for duration
STOP.auxiliary: Balance speakers and paraphrases so the largest source cannot determine checkpoint selection

NEXT.collection: Record Next, Skip, Skip song and Play next song with distinct speakers and speaking rates
NEXT.review: Keep the next/skip cue in acoustic targets; do not relabel a next-song command as generic play
contrasts: single next command vs multi-action sentence
NEXT.segmentation: Retain the final consonant cluster in Next and the cue in Play next song
NEXT.auxiliary: Evaluate short and connected variants separately

VOLUME.collection: Fill up/down/mute/set operations and approved numeric values with connected human utterances; oversample scarce typed cells rather than just the family
VOLUME.review: Keep absolute to X distinct from relative by X. Review play-it-louder rather than blindly applying an unapproved color/volume proposal
contrasts: volume up vs down vs mute
fifteen vs fifty; sixteen vs sixty
valid set value vs missing/negative/over-100 value
VOLUME.segmentation: Preserve the complete number and percent/unit; never construct commands by concatenating numeral clips
VOLUME.auxiliary: Only original-human train-only number clips may support an explicit auxiliary ablation; they do not close connected percentage gaps

CALL.collection: Add generic/default-home and mom/mother commands with disjoint train/dev/calibration speakers; review existing excluded human CALL metadata first
CALL.review: Generic Call may use the approved Home default; explicit unknown contacts and incomplete Call to must reject. Do not invent a contact
CALL.segmentation: Retain utterance-final contact; a correct call family with the wrong person is a full-command failure
CALL.auxiliary: Two training speakers are not broad contact generalization; no test-speaker enrollment

MESSAGE.collection: Find or record original human Message/Send a message/Send my message utterances with empty slots and independent fitting/development/calibration speakers
MESSAGE.review: Existing recipient/body-bearing MESSAGE recordings are not automatically valid empty-slot positives. Missing eligible positives remains a blocker
contrasts: supported request vs unknown recipient or conflicting message content
MESSAGE.segmentation: Preserve the send/message cue without discarding appended unsupported content
MESSAGE.auxiliary: No synthetic examples, label rewrites or decoder aliases may be counted as human coverage

LIST_REMINDERS.collection: Add original human calibration positives and diversify list/show/read-my-reminders wording
LIST_REMINDERS.review: Keep listing distinct from creating or deleting reminders; arbitrary requested list scopes are not silently ignored
contrasts: list/show reminders vs remind me to task
LIST_REMINDERS.segmentation: Preserve list/show/read and terminal plural; noun-only Reminders remains a distinct acoustic stratum
LIST_REMINDERS.auxiliary: Do not fit a low threshold when this human calibration class is absent

TIMER.collection: Fill connected duration cells, particularly baseline ten seconds, thirty seconds and one minute, across independent speakers; include seconds/minutes/hours only within the frozen catalog
TIMER.review: Adjudicate transcript versus slot_value conflicts by original-audio listening. Do not train six disputed duration labels or infer units from the coarse family
contrasts: timer duration vs alarm clock time
TIMER.segmentation: Retain units and pauses between number and unit; test the 400 ms endpoint on natural pauses before adopting a trim
TIMER.auxiliary: Train-only human duration/token auxiliaries require source/speaker/PCM exclusions and their own supervision mask

ALARM.collection: Fill independent speakers for each approved clock cell, especially morning/evening contrasts and permitted non-hour times
ALARM.review: Keep explicit AM/PM and Asia/Manila semantics. Missing meridiem, conflicting time or unrepresented recurrence must not be defaulted
contrasts: alarm clock time vs timer duration
noon/midnight only if approved and annotated
ALARM.segmentation: Preserve quiet final A M/P M; review internal pauses before meridiem for premature endpointing
ALARM.auxiliary: Clock phoneme/token coverage does not equal complete typed alarm coverage

TEMPERATURE.collection: Add train/development speakers beyond the few existing people and a separate human calibration population; fill baseline 18/22/26 C cells
TEMPERATURE.review: Verify degrees/unit and keep invalid bounds, missing values and Fahrenheit requests separate under the existing C-only contract
TEMPERATURE.segmentation: Retain complete numeral and degree/unit suffix; do not rely on source microphone identity
TEMPERATURE.auxiliary: Report leave-source-out diagnostics on development; no synthetic accent label counts as a human accent

BRIGHTNESS.collection: Expand the one-example human dev set and missing calibration values. Fill baseline 20/60/100 percent, then the approved target/value matrix with separate speakers
BRIGHTNESS.review: Preserve absolute percent and named light jointly; review brightness/colour/power conflicts. 0-100 text support is not 101 spoken human values
contrasts: twenty vs sixty vs one hundred
absolute to vs unsupported relative by
BRIGHTNESS.segmentation: Keep the full number and target; screen long silence without truncating quiet initial brightness or final percent
BRIGHTNESS.auxiliary: Connected percentage data takes precedence over isolated numbers; no word splicing

COLOR.collection: Fill every approved color/light pair with independent speakers, including warm white versus cool white and scarce named targets
COLOR.review: Honor the parent's rejected annotation proposals. Blue lights please and similar activation-versus-color ambiguities require review, not unconditional relabeling
contrasts: set color vs turn on an already colored light
COLOR.segmentation: Retain color adjectives and terminal target; never replace a two-word color by its final white token
COLOR.auxiliary: Balance the color-target joint cell and source, not marginal color counts alone

CREATE_REMINDER.collection: Add separate speakers for drink-water, study and exercise and original human calibration positives; first review existing unsupported/ambiguous task metadata
CREATE_REMINDER.review: One training speaker/task cannot establish task recognition. Preserve the approved finite task scope; do not erase dictated content or pretend arbitrary reminders are supported
contrasts: study vs exercise vs drink water
CREATE_REMINDER.segmentation: Retain the entire task phrase after remind me to, including quiet utterance endings
CREATE_REMINDER.auxiliary: Independent enrollment/task recordings cannot share evaluation speakers, sessions or parent audio

UNKNOWN.collection: Record human near-command negatives: negation, unknown names/targets, malformed numbers, unsupported units/content, multi-command requests, conversation and background/no-speech sessions
UNKNOWN.review: Ambiguous/unintelligible references stay unscored quarantine, not true UNKNOWN. Distinguish unsupported semantics from capture faults and incomplete supervision
contrasts: capture fault vs intelligible out-of-scope speech
UNKNOWN.segmentation: Preserve negative qualifiers and all appended content. Silence/clipping screens do not create semantic negative labels
UNKNOWN.auxiliary: Report false accepts with the true-negative denominator and confidence intervals. Use a new blind human population for acceptance claims
